 # REST and scripting APIs
+
+Schema 33 introduces prepared `WetPaintStroke` values through existing `paint.add`, `layer.add` and raster `layer.update.erasures` commands. No new REST simulation/render endpoint is added. A wet record contains `id`, `kind:"wet"`, independent `opacity` (0–1), `clip:null`, brush/pencil `brush` metadata, normalized `load`/`mix`, invertible `nativeTransform`, and native `tiles:[{x,y,width,height,assetId,coverage:{assetId}}]`. See [the constructor contract and runnable isolated example](SCRIPTING_API.md#prepared-wet-paint-schema-33). Native pixels are authoritative; metadata does not execute a brush engine on the server.
+
+Upload prepared output/coverage PNGs using the existing assets endpoint, then reference their returned IDs. Both must have matching actual tile dimensions; output alpha must already be masked and cannot exceed coverage alpha. Validation finishes before the synchronous transaction and rechecks session/revision. Invalid content returns 400 without partial edits; stale revisions return 409. Existing locks, batches and undo apply. The headless alpha decoder supports noninterlaced RGB8/RGBA8 PNGs with unmarked/sRGB color; ICC/APNG and other unsupported declarations reject explicitly. Browser decoding can accept additional declarations; this explicit headless limit is not a browser import restriction. Existing REST body/upload budgets apply, and sessions remain independent of the browser.
 
 Both are required product surfaces. They share the same OOP document model, command validation and history behavior. Neither is a Photoshop-compatible API. These are local prototype APIs, not a published SDK stability guarantee.

 # Architecture
+
+### Prepared wet-paint authoring (schema 33, verification in progress)
+
+`core/wet-operation.ts` defines distinct prepared replacements rather than colored brush dabs. Output is premasked in native pixels; coverage removes destination and output adds once. Independent operation opacity envelopes the completed replacement once. Paint uses ordered strokes; raster retains its original source and ordered erasure log with captured geometry. Central asset visitors include output, coverage and nested brush textures for persistence/remapping/source capture/history.
+
+`engine/wet-authoring.ts` prepares complete native spatial output privately through the actual worker/WASM engine. Sampling uses neutral target content before layer/parent appearance, with raster native pixels independent of logical size. Selection, revision, session and source lifetime guard publication. Backing storage releases before publication; PNG dimensions/alpha validate before shared OO commands commit once. Private assets publish only at that synchronous boundary. This adapter does not implement interactive mixer/smudge gestures, incremental previews, mask/filter-mask targets or presets.
+
+`core/wet-assets.ts` checks premasked alpha through bounded asynchronous streams, identity guards and content proofs. Browser/script commits and independent REST commands share the invariant, with the server's explicit sRGB8 PNG decoder limits. Script cancellation, time, revisions and grants are rechecked before private retouch assets publish; no new host privilege is exposed. `wet-native.ts` reconstructs content on bounded native surfaces with interpolation halos/integer output clips before transforms/appearance. GPU capability rejects wet content for complete fallback; SVG prepares disclosed native sibling prefixes. SCRIPTING_API.md defines exact defaults/errors/limits. The [authored integration evidence](benchmarks/brush-wet-authoring-2026-10-18.json) records the verification boundary.

+## Prepared wet paint (schema 33)
+
+`new WetPaintStroke({brush, tiles, nativeTransform?, opacity?, load?, mix?})` creates an immutable prepared replacement value. Add it to `PaintLayer.strokes`, or call `RasterLayer.applyWetPaint(stroke): void`. Raster replacements retain their order relative to erase/clear, capture the current logical width/height, and preserve the original image asset. Attached mutations use ordinary commands, ancestor locks, transactions and undo. DTOs use `kind: "wet"` and require schema 33, including retained history and embedded masters. Older valid documents migrate; falsely old wet records reject. Project v3/workspace v2 are unchanged.
+
+`brush` is a `BrushStroke`/`PencilStroke` value or its complete DTO, without clone tiles. It records the footprint, path, captured selection, opacity, flow, pressure, tilt, symmetry and optional texture. These settings describe preparation: **the supplied pixels are authoritative**, and editing metadata does not rerun the simulation. Eraser/clone/fill footprints reject. `tiles` is a nonempty array of `{x,y,width,height,assetId,coverage:{assetId}}`. Geometry is integral native pixels with positive extents and safe numeric addressing. `nativeTransform` maps native tile coordinates into layer-local coordinates and defaults to identity. Independent operation `opacity` defaults to 1 and blends the complete replacement once, including overlapping tiles. The brush's opacity/selection must already be baked into supplied pixels; outer DTO `clip` is always null.
+
+Both image references must resolve to decoded, noninterlaced RGB8/RGBA8 PNG assets whose actual dimensions match their tile. Output alpha must be at most coverage alpha at every native pixel: output is already masked, coverage removes destination pixels, and output is added once. This permits reducing alpha. Coverage RGB is ignored. Browser/script commits and REST decode/check native alpha before publishing; invalid/missing/replaced sources reject the entire transaction. This derived-output contract does not restrict original-image or brush-texture import formats/resolution. Native tile coordinates, count and original dimensions have no arbitrary image-tier cap; working buffers, storage quota and numeric/format precision can still fail explicitly.
+
+`load` accepts `{color?: [r,g,b,a], load?: number}`; channels are integral 0–255 and load is 0–1, defaulting to opaque black and 0. `mix` accepts `{flow?,wetness?,pickup?}`, each 0–1, defaulting to 1/0/0.5. Unknown keys/nonfinite or out-of-range values reject. These normalized settings are retained metadata on prepared values. Read-only members are `id`, `kind`, `opacity`, `brush`, `tiles`, `nativeTransform`, `load`, `mix`, and `toJSON()`; returned arrays/DTOs are owned copies.
+
+This isolated example requires two already imported PNG image layers named **Wet output** and **Wet coverage**, with matching original pixel dimensions and valid premasked output. Source layers are kept as imported; use hidden source layers if their images should appear only in the replacement. No files, pixels, native simulation or export service is exposed to the sandbox.
+
+<!-- example: wet-prepared -->
+
+```js
+const output = [...document.layers].find(layer => layer.name === 'Wet output');
+const coverage = [...document.layers].find(layer => layer.name === 'Wet coverage');
+if (!(output instanceof RasterLayer) || !(coverage instanceof RasterLayer)) {
+  throw new Error('Import Wet output and Wet coverage PNG images first.');
+}
+const paint = new PaintLayer({name: 'Prepared wet paint'});
+paint.strokes.add(new WetPaintStroke({
+  brush: new PencilStroke({points: [{x: 3.5, y: 4.5}], pressureSize: false}),
+  tiles: [{x: 3, y: 4, width: output.width, height: output.height,
+    assetId: output.assetId, coverage: {assetId: coverage.assetId}}]
+}));
+document.layers.add(paint);
+print('Prepared wet paint ready');
+```
+
+Use original dimensions without resizing the two source layers. The host validates actual decoded dimensions and alpha, rather than trusting their display geometry. Plugins need their existing `document:write` grant; installation remains inert, and no new permission/file/network boundary is added. Browser rendering composes replacements on a native content plane before layer transforms/appearance. Unsupported GPU compositions use complete Canvas fallback. SVG bakes affected paint-layer sibling prefixes and discloses lost editability; save a project for complete sources and operations.
+
+### Wet preparation (trusted application code)
+
+`await editor.applyWetPaint(brush, options?): Promise<WetPaintStroke|null>` runs actual native spatial preparation and atomically commits the result. `brush` is a BrushStroke/PencilStroke whose coordinates are **target-local**, while captured document selection is transformed into that plane. `options` accepts only `mode?: "smudge"|"mixer"` (default smudge), `targetId?: string` (default selected layer), `respectSelection?: boolean` (default true), `load?`, `mix?`, `signal?: AbortSignal`, and `onProgress?: ({dabs,workingTiles}) => void`. An explicit brush clip takes precedence over document selection; false respectSelection clears both. With no selected target it creates a paint layer; other target kinds or locked ancestry reject.
+
+Preparation samples the target's neutral content, including preceding ordered operations, before its opacity/mask/styles/tone effects or parent appearance. Raster sampling uses original pixels independently of current logical size; source blobs remain unchanged. Foreground defaults to the brush's opaque RGB. Smudge defaults load to 0 and wetness to 0; mixer defaults load to 1 and wetness to 0.25. Partial load/mix options override those mode defaults; remaining mix flow/pickup defaults are 1/0.5. This is finite encoded-sRGB pigment transport, not a physical/spectral model.
+
+```js
+const stroke = new PencilStroke({
+  points: [{x: 10.5, y: 20.5}, {x: 30.5, y: 20.5}],
+  size: 3, pressureSize: false, color: '#ff0000'
+});
+const result = await editor.applyWetPaint(stroke, {
+  mode: 'mixer', mix: {wetness: 0, pickup: 0}, signal: controller.signal
+});
+```
+
+Import constructors from the host DOM module and provide an AbortController as `controller`. No changed pixels returns null without history/assets. Abort, callback errors, quota/source-lifetime failures or changed document/revision/active selection/session reject without late publication. Private storage is disposed before commit; staged assets publish only after validation and remain for undo/redo. Original-first symmetry order, separate spatial pigment per copy, once-only selection/brush opacity, native replacement and complete path replay are preserved. Numerical work uses at most 4 million pixels/request and native composition at most 4 million pixels/4096 pixels per side per working surface; these are working budgets, not source limits. This adapter does not implement incremental live gestures, mixer/smudge tool controls, mask/filter-mask painting or preset integration. Those roadmap gates remain open.
+
 ## Maintaining this contract
 
 Update this guide whenever a constructor, public member, default, validation rule, runtime binding, budget or history behavior changes. Keep the [API overview](API.md), [requirements](REQUIREMENTS.md) and [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) consistent. Keep examples runnable in the Scripts panel without invented assets or page globals.

--- before/docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md
+++ after/docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md
@@ -1,4 +1,6 @@
 # Canoli Studio System Design & Architecture Specification
+
+Schema-33 prepared wet operations preserve ordered native pixel replacement before layer appearance. Output alpha is at most coverage alpha and is already masked; coverage removes destination alpha and output adds once. Whole-operation opacity envelopes all replacements once. Never mask already filtered output a second time or convert original rasters to paint layers. Source pixels and captured operation geometry survive resize/undo/persistence. Bounded native reconstruction precedes transforms; GPU falls back and SVG uses disclosed native prefixes. Async preparation/validation owns private resources and rechecks revision/session/selection/source identity before a synchronous OO commit. Scripts and REST share prepared-content validation within existing isolation/session boundaries. This adapter is in verification; gestures, incremental previews and full tool/preset/mask/performance gates remain open.
 
 Native spatial wet preparation processes the complete recorded path before viewport cropping. Each symmetry copy owns a separate native spatial pigment field; copies sample completed preceding copies in shared dab order. Within one dab, all destination and carried reads use the same prior epoch. Complete private staging precedes advancement, and bilinear neighbors sum in a fixed order across backing partitions. Native coverage uses a fixed raster grid; final opacity/selection applies once and unchanged pixels remain byte-invariant. Disk-backed private jobs survive resident cache eviction, and active Web Locks prevent abandoned-job cleanup from deleting another tab/worker's state. Failed preparation publishes no model/assets and deletes its own namespace; completed output owns its bytes until disposal. The rendered-document sampler captures source/font identity and remains read-only. These are internal dependencies; authored ordered layer replacement, OO/history/persistence, tools/preview and export/automation integration remain unfinished. See ARCHITECTURE.md for defaults, bounds, cleanup fallback and current limits.
